description: WaRF validation corpus — controlled mutations with pre-certified ground truth. Each session has a known x* established before any agent is queried. Used to verify synthesis function correctness, Bayesian weight convergence direction, and SPRT stopping behaviour.

sessions.label: Clean baseline — no mutation
sessions.review_prompt: Review the following C++ code for logical correctness, edge-case handling, and type safety. Vote APPROVE (+1) if the code is correct and complete. Vote REJECT (-1) if you identify a defect. Provide a brief rationale.

ground_truth.rationale: Original unmodified code. Division-by-zero guard is present. Casts are correct. All tests pass. Expected verdict: APPROVE.

sessions.label: Removed division-by-zero guard
sessions.review_prompt: Review the following C++ code for logical correctness, edge-case handling, and type safety. Vote APPROVE (+1) if the code is correct and complete. Vote REJECT (-1) if you identify a defect. Provide a brief rationale.

secondary_oracle.note: ctest divide-by-zero test case would crash or produce UB

ground_truth.rationale: The if (b == 0) guard and std::invalid_argument throw have been removed. Calling divide(x, 0) produces undefined behaviour (integer division by zero). Expected verdict: REJECT.

sessions.label: SFINAE syntax error — missing _t on enable_if
sessions.review_prompt: Review the following C++ code for logical correctness, edge-case handling, and type safety. Pay particular attention to template and type-trait usage. Vote APPROVE (+1) if the code is correct and complete. Vote REJECT (-1) if you identify a defect. Provide a brief rationale.

secondary_oracle.note: CMake build fails: lambda return type resolves to the enable_if struct, not void

ground_truth.rationale: std::enable_if<condition, void> returns the struct itself, not the nested type. The correct form is std::enable_if_t<condition, void> or std::enable_if<condition, void>::type. Without this, the lambda has an invalid return type and the code fails to compile. Expected verdict: REJECT.

sessions.label: Missing edge-case test coverage
sessions.review_prompt: Review the following Python test suite for adequacy of coverage. Consider whether edge cases, negative inputs, and boundary conditions are tested. Vote APPROVE (+1) if the coverage is sufficient. Vote REJECT (-1) if significant gaps exist. Provide a brief rationale.

ground_truth.rationale: Negative-operand cases removed from test_add and test_subtract. No test for multiply with negative inputs or zero. No test for subtract producing a negative result. These gaps mean integer sign-handling bugs in the implementation would not be caught by CI. Expected verdict: REJECT. Note: automated tools (pylint, mypy, pytest) will all pass — only a human reviewer can identify coverage gaps.

sessions.label: Path traversal via unsanitized user input
sessions.review_prompt: Review the following Python code for security vulnerabilities, with particular attention to input handling and file system access. Vote APPROVE (+1) if the code is secure. Vote REJECT (-1) if you identify a security defect. Provide a brief rationale.

ground_truth.rationale: filename is user-controlled and passed directly to os.path.join without sanitization. A value like ../../etc/passwd allows reading arbitrary files outside base_dir. Fix: use os.path.basename(filename) before joining, then verify the resolved path starts with os.path.realpath(base_dir). Expected verdict: REJECT.

sessions.label: O(n) loop division instead of O(1)
sessions.review_prompt: Review the following C++ code for performance correctness and algorithmic efficiency. Vote APPROVE (+1) if the implementation is acceptably efficient. Vote REJECT (-1) if you identify a significant performance defect. Provide a brief rationale.

secondary_oracle.note: divide(INT_MAX, 1) would loop ~2 billion times; measurable regression vs O(1) baseline

ground_truth.rationale: Division implemented via repeated subtraction loop. Time complexity is O(|a/b|) instead of O(1). divide(INT_MAX, 1) iterates ~2.1 billion times. The loop also loses fractional precision — it only returns an integer quotient cast to double, discarding the remainder. Two independent defects: algorithmic complexity and precision loss. Expected verdict: REJECT.

sessions.label: Silent integer overflow in multiply
sessions.review_prompt: Review the following C++ code for logical correctness and safety. Consider arithmetic edge cases and undefined behaviour. Vote APPROVE (+1) if the code is correct and safe. Vote REJECT (-1) if you identify a defect. Provide a brief rationale.

secondary_oracle.note: A ctest case for multiply(INT_MAX, 2) would expose UB via sanitizer (-fsanitize=undefined)

ground_truth.rationale: multiply(a, b) performs a * b with no overflow check. In C++, signed integer overflow is undefined behaviour. multiply(INT_MAX, 2) silently wraps to a negative value on most platforms. The misleading comment 'validated for typical inputs' may cause agents to approve without deeper analysis. A correct implementation would check: if (b != 0 && a > INT_MAX / b) throw std::overflow_error. Expected verdict: REJECT.
